_comment: Drives test/klippy/multi_mcu_linuxprocess_avr.test under a mixed simavr (atmega2560) + native linuxprocess multi-bridge fan-out. The runner spawns the simavr bridge for the AVR main and the linuxprocess klipper.elf directly (the linux mcu opens its own pty via openpty() and symlinks the slave end). tick_mode is DISABLED here on purpose: the linuxprocess mcu runs on the real wall clock with no sim-time hook, and the runner only tick-sockets the simavr bridge -- so under tick_mode klippy's monotonic (get_monotonic reads the AVR bridge's sim-time mmap) would stamp the wall-clock linuxprocess mcu's clocksync responses with AVR sim-time, diverging the two clocks and intermittently failing the run (the same AVR-vs-real-time divergence as the AVR + renode mix). With tick_mode false both backends and klippy share the real wall clock, so clocksync behaves as on real hardware. auto_trsync_trigger_ticks fires the X/Y/Z endstops after 100 step edges so G28 completes; the fixture pusher routes those step_trigger commands to the AVR bridge's control socket since all stepper pins are on [mcu], and skips the linuxprocess bridge entirely (no control socket on the linuxprocess backend -- peripheral state is staged via filesystem mocks before spawn).
